question: Why was the customary interest on Babylonian silver loans exactly 20% a year?
answer: Because of the arithmetic of their units. The standard charge was one shekel per mina per month, and a mina held 60 shekels: 1/60 a month, 12/60 a year. Barley loans ran at a third. The same 20% recurs in law codes and contracts across a thousand years: money priced by a counting system.
move: Before explaining a number, check whether the counting system chose it.
source: Homer and Sylla, A History of Interest Rates
reference: Homer & Sylla, A History of Interest Rates, 4th edition, Wiley, 2005
